title: Buck Mulligan
html_source:
Joyce based this character on his acquaintance, Oliver St. John Gogarty. Joyce’s Trieste Notebook from 1909 contains an entry on Gogarty, complete with phrases which would go on to appear in Ulysses. For instance, the sentence

The Omphalos was to be the temple of a neo-paganism.

Would turn up in

To ourselves… new paganism… omphalos.

a bit later in this chapter.

Both men had suffered a falling out, hence Joyce’s critical depiction. Gogarty was a poet, an author, a politician, but above all else a conversationalist. Joyce’s opinion on whether or not he was successful at any of those occupations is fairly clear from the text.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: Gogarty was also importantly a doctor (and Joyce himself spent some time as a medical student in Paris); at the time of the setting of Ulysses, Buck Mulligan is a medical student.
